```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
os.environ["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# execution cwd is the report dir (quarto) or the repo root; walk up to the repo
BASE = Path(".").resolve()
while not (BASE / "src").exists() and BASE != BASE.parent:
    BASE = BASE.parent
if not (BASE / "src").exists():
    BASE = Path(".").resolve()
DB = Path.home() / ".prime" / "agent" / "data_manager.db"

conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB}?mode=ro", uri=True)
conn.execute("PRAGMA cache_size=-65536")     # 256MB page cache
conn.execute("PRAGMA mmap_size=134217728")   # 128MB mmap reads
conn.execute("PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY")
conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=20000")

_styl = next((s for s in (Path.cwd() / "report.mplstyle",
                            BASE / "report" / "report.mplstyle") if s.exists()), None)
if _styl is not None:
    plt.style.use(str(_styl))
plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "serif", "font.size": 10,
                     "axes.titlesize": 10.5, "axes.labelsize": 9.5,
                     "axes.edgecolor": "#333", "axes.linewidth": .7,
                     "grid.alpha": .25, "figure.facecolor": "white",
                     "axes.facecolor": "white"})
NAVY = "#1f3b63"; GOLD = "#c9a227"; LIGHT = "#eef1f5"; GRAY = "#b0b4bb"; RED = "#a94e4e"

def q(sql, params=()):
    return pd.read_sql(sql, conn, params=params)

def fmt(x):
    return f"{int(x):,}"
```

::: {style="background:#eef1f5;border-left:5px solid #1f3b63;padding:14px 18px;border-radius:4px;"}
**Abstract.** `~/.prime/agent/data_manager.db` is the single local SQLite
source of point-in-time market data for the quant stack — 61.7M as-traded
daily price rows (stocks and funds) back to 1998, a 3.15M-row SF1
fundamentals mirror (six report dimensions), the full Sharadar securities
master (31,742 instruments, survivorship-free), corporate actions (670k
rows incl. delistings), and a point-in-time investable-universe table
(`universe_pit`) holding **13.46M stock-days across 7,187 trading days**
(1998-01-14 → 2026-08-11). The database is loaded from Sharadar bulk files
(~2 GB of zips, zero per-ticker API fan-out), WAL-mode, index-tuned for
cross-sectional scans, and passed a full `integrity_check` + `VACUUM`
(17.1 → 15.9 GB) on 2026-08-11. This report documents coverage, depth, and
the data-quality findings that matter for consumers (eqrm,
stock-selection, backtests). All numbers are as of the last warehouse
build on 2026-08-11.
:::

# Warehouse at a glance

```{python}
#| label: counts
counts = q("""
 SELECT 'prices' t, COUNT(*) n, MIN(date) lo, MAX(date) hi FROM prices
 UNION ALL SELECT 'sf1', COUNT(*), MIN(date), MAX(date) FROM sf1
 UNION ALL SELECT 'fundamentals', COUNT(*), MIN(fiscal_year), MAX(fiscal_year) FROM fundamentals
 UNION ALL SELECT 'quarterly_statements', COUNT(*), MIN(period), MAX(period) FROM quarterly_statements
 UNION ALL SELECT 'ratios', COUNT(*), MIN(as_of), MAX(as_of) FROM ratios
 UNION ALL SELECT 'metrics', COUNT(*), MIN(as_of), MAX(as_of) FROM metrics
 UNION ALL SELECT 'securities_master', COUNT(*), NULL, NULL FROM securities_master
 UNION ALL SELECT 'corporate_actions', COUNT(*), MIN(date), MAX(date) FROM corporate_actions
 UNION ALL SELECT 'sp500_membership', COUNT(*), MIN(date), MAX(date) FROM sp500_membership
 UNION ALL SELECT 'universe_pit', COUNT(*), MIN(as_of), MAX(as_of) FROM universe_pit
""")
overview = counts.rename(columns={"t": "table", "n": "rows", "lo": "first", "hi": "last"})
overview["rows"] = overview["rows"].map(fmt)
overview["first"] = overview["first"].fillna("—")
overview["last"] = overview["last"].fillna("—")
overview
```

# Price coverage & depth

Daily as-traded OHLCV plus a total-return adjustment factor
($P^{\mathrm{adj}}_t = P^{\mathrm{as\text{-}traded}}_t \times \mathrm{adjustment}_t$),
**survivorship-free** — delisted names stay in the table. The stocks-vs-funds
split uses the bulk-file origin (`securities_master.table`).

```{python}
#| label: yearscan
# one 61.7M-row pass: quotes per calendar year, stocks vs funds + date bounds
years = q("""
 SELECT substr(p.date,1,4) AS yr, m.`table` AS kind,
        COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ticker) AS tickers
 FROM prices p LEFT JOIN securities_master m ON m.ticker = p.ticker
 GROUP BY yr, kind ORDER BY yr
""")
pivot = years.pivot(index="yr", columns="kind", values="n").fillna(0)
ptick = years.pivot(index="yr", columns="kind", values="tickers").fillna(0)
bounds = years.groupby("kind").agg(rows=("n", "sum"))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig_coverage
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.2
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2))
yrs = pivot.index.astype(int).values
ax1.bar(yrs, pivot["stocks"], color=NAVY, width=0.8, label="stocks")
ax1.bar(yrs, pivot["funds"], bottom=pivot["stocks"], color=GOLD, width=0.8, label="funds")
ax1.set_yscale("log"); ax1.set_ylim(1e4, 1e8)
ax1.set_title("Daily price rows per calendar year (log)")
ax1.set_xlabel("year"); ax1.set_ylabel("rows")
ax1.legend(frameon=False); ax1.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25)
ax2.plot(yrs, ptick["stocks"], "-o", color=NAVY, ms=3, lw=1.4, label="stocks")
ax2.plot(yrs, ptick["funds"], "-o", color=GOLD, ms=3, lw=1.4, label="funds")
ax2.set_title("Distinct quoted tickers per year")
ax2.set_xlabel("year"); ax2.set_ylabel("tickers")
ax2.legend(frameon=False); ax2.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: bounds_prose
lo_s = years[years.kind == "stocks"].iloc[0]["yr"] + "-01"
lo_f = years[years.kind == "funds"].iloc[0]["yr"] + "-01"
display(Markdown(
    f"Coverage is continuous for stocks from **{lo_s}** ({fmt(bounds.loc['stocks','rows'])} rows) "
    f"and for funds from **{lo_f}** ({fmt(bounds.loc['funds','rows'])} rows). Stock coverage runs "
    "**~8,000–9,000 quoted tickers/year from 1998 onward** (delisted names included, so yearly "
    f"counts are *quoted* securities, not survivors); fund coverage grows from a few hundred to "
    f"**{fmt(ptick['funds'].max())}** tickers after 2010. The {fmt(int(pivot.loc['1997'].sum()))}-row "
    "1997 sliver is a bulk-file edge (pre-window rows for a handful of names), consistent with the "
    "Sharadar per-ticker window cap of ~28.6y noted at migration time."))
```

# Point-in-time investable universe

`universe_pit` is rebuilt locally from master + prices + SF1 (zero API
calls): a (date, member) row exists iff, *as of that date*, the security was
a Domestic Common Stock (Primary/Secondary), last as-traded close ≥ $2,
trailing 20-day average dollar volume ≥ $5M (≥ 10 sessions), PIT market cap
(price × latest as-reported shares) ≥ $300M, and the quote was fresh
(≤ 10 calendar days old).

```{python}
#| label: pit_series
pit = q("SELECT as_of, COUNT(*) n FROM universe_pit GROUP BY as_of ORDER BY as_of")
pit["as_of"] = pd.to_datetime(pit["as_of"])
pit_row = int(pit["n"].sum()); pit_days = len(pit)
anchor_days = ("1998-01-14", "2020-03-23", "2021-08-10", "2024-12-31")
anchors = pit[pit["as_of"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d").isin(anchor_days)].copy()
anchors["label"] = anchors["as_of"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
latest = pit.iloc[-1]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig_pit
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.8
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3.8))
ax.fill_between(pit["as_of"], pit["n"], color=LIGHT, lw=0)
ax.plot(pit["as_of"], pit["n"], color=NAVY, lw=1.1)
ax.axvspan(pd.Timestamp("2021-08-10"), pd.Timestamp("2024-12-31"),
           color=GOLD, alpha=.18, label="eqrm modelling window")
ax.plot(latest["as_of"], latest["n"], "o", color=RED, ms=5)
for _, r in anchors.iterrows():
    ax.plot(r["as_of"], r["n"], "o", color=RED, ms=4)
    ax.annotate(f"{r['label']}  {r['n']:,}", (r["as_of"], r["n"]),
                textcoords="offset points", xytext=(4, 7), fontsize=8, color=RED)
ax.annotate(f"{latest['as_of'].date()}  {latest['n']:,}", (latest["as_of"], latest["n"]),
            textcoords="offset points", xytext=(-4, -14), fontsize=8, color=RED)
ax.set_title(f"Investable-universe membership per trading day — {pit_days:,} days, {pit_row:,} stock-days")
ax.set_xlabel("date"); ax.set_ylabel("members"); ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: pit_prose
a0 = anchors[anchors.label == "1998-01-14"].iloc[0]
grow = latest["n"] / a0["n"]
display(Markdown(
    f"Membership grows from **{fmt(a0['n'])}** names on 1998-01-14 to "
    f"**{fmt(latest['n'])}** on the latest day ({latest['as_of'].date().isoformat()}) — "
    f"**{grow:.1f}×** — with a structural step in the mid-2000s as NASDAQ/NYSE listing "
    "standards pushed names through the $5M-volume screen, and the 2020 crash bottom at "
    f"**{fmt(anchors[anchors.label=='2020-03-23'].iloc[0]['n'])}** members (2020-03-23). The "
    f"~2,400 current members sit **below** the ~3,000 Russell-styled target because the "
    "trailing-dollar-volume and $300M-mcap screens use *as-reported* shares; "
    "`build-universe-pit` thresholds are re-runnable to compare variants."))
last_day = latest["as_of"].date().isoformat()
sec = q("SELECT sector, COUNT(*) n FROM universe_pit WHERE as_of=?", (last_day,))
exch = q("SELECT exchange, COUNT(*) n FROM universe_pit WHERE as_of=?", (last_day,))
cat = q("SELECT category, COUNT(*) n FROM universe_pit GROUP BY category").sort_values("n", ascending=False)
sec["n"] = sec["n"].map(fmt); exch["n"] = exch["n"].map(fmt)
cat["pct"] = (100 * cat["n"] / cat["n"].sum()).round(1).map(lambda v: f"{v}%")
sec.columns = ["sector (Sharadar taxonomy)", "members"]
exch.columns = ["exchange", "members"]
cat.columns = ["category (all days)", "stock-days", "share"]
display(Markdown(f"**Latest-day composition ({last_day}).**"))
pd.concat([sec.reset_index(drop=True), exch.reset_index(drop=True)], axis=1)
```

```{python}
#| label: pit_constitution
display(cat.reset_index(drop=True))
display(Markdown(
    "The constitution check confirms the PIT gate admits **only Domestic Common Stock "
    "(incl. Primary class)** — no ETF, ADR, preferred, or warrant rows ever enter "
    "(fails closed, per the eqrm positive inclusion-filter design)."))
```

# Securities master composition

The whole Sharadar `tickers` table: 31,742 instruments (21,960 stocks,
9,782 funds), of which **19,227 (60.6%) are delisted** — the
survivorship-free core of the warehouse.

```{python}
#| label: fig_cats
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
cats = q("SELECT category, COUNT(*) n FROM securities_master GROUP BY category ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 14")
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4))
c = cats.iloc[::-1]
y = np.arange(len(c))
ax1.barh(y, c["n"], color=NAVY, height=0.7)
ax1.set_yticks(y, c["category"], fontsize=8.5)
ax1.set_title("Securities master — top categories")
ax1.set_xlabel("instruments"); ax1.grid(axis="x", alpha=.25)
d = q("SELECT isdelisted, COUNT(*) n FROM securities_master GROUP BY 1").set_index("isdelisted")
ax2.bar(["active (N)"], [d.loc["N", "n"]], color=NAVY)
ax2.bar(["delisted (Y)"], [d.loc["Y", "n"]], color=RED)
ax2.set_title("Survivorship split (N = 12,515 / Y = 19,227)")
ax2.set_ylabel("instruments"); ax2.grid(axis="y", alpha=.25)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

# GICS classification coverage

`classifications` carries the eqrm gate: the eleven GICS labels mapped from
Sharadar's taxonomy. **Coverage is a known gap** — only the iShares-era
universe (2,589 names) is classified, not the full 21,960-stock master;
`securities_master.sector/industry` (Sharadar taxonomy) covers every
instrument but uses non-GICS labels (e.g. *Healthcare* vs *Health Care*).
The NOTES.md action item — a live GICS-map coverage check against the whole
master — remains open.

```{python}
#| label: fig_gics
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.6
g = q("SELECT sector, COUNT(*) n FROM classifications GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.6))
gg = g.iloc[::-1]
y = np.arange(len(gg))
cols = [GOLD if s == "Cash and/or Derivatives" else NAVY for s in gg["sector"]]
ax.barh(y, gg["n"], color=cols, height=0.72)
ax.set_yticks(y, gg["sector"], fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_title("GICS-mapped classifications (2,589 iShares-era names)")
ax.set_xlabel("names"); ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=.25)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: gics_cover
cov = q("""SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM classifications) classified,
                  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM securities_master WHERE `table`='stocks') stocks_master""").iloc[0]
display(Markdown(
    f"Classified names: **{fmt(cov['classified'])}** of **{fmt(cov['stocks_master'])}** "
    f"stocks in the master (**{100*cov['classified']/cov['stocks_master']:.1f}%** coverage). "
    "No NULL sectors; the five *Cash and/or Derivatives* rows are iShares IWV placeholders "
    "that carry no GICS sector and are excluded from the eqrm allowlist by construction."))
```

# Freshness & data quality

```{python}
#| label: quality
qc = q("""
 SELECT COUNT(*) total,
        SUM(volume = 0) vol0,
        SUM(adjustment > 100) adj_hi,
        SUM(adjustment < 0.01) adj_lo,
        SUM(close <= 0) close_le0,
        SUM(volume = 0 AND adjustment > 100) vol0_adj_hi
 FROM prices
""").T.rename(columns={0: "rows"})
qc["pct"] = (100 * qc["rows"] / qc.loc["total", "rows"]).round(2)
qc.loc["total", "pct"] = 100.0
qc["rows"] = qc["rows"].map(fmt)
qc["pct"] = qc["pct"].map(lambda v: f"{v:.2f}%")
qc.index = ["all rows", "volume = 0 (no-trade days)", "adjustment > 100",
            "adjustment < 0.01", "close ≤ 0",
            "volume = 0 AND adjustment > 100 (sentinel)"]
qc.columns = ["rows", "% of total"]
qc
```

```{python}
#| label: adj_extremes
ext = q("""
 SELECT ticker, date, close, volume, adjustment
 FROM prices WHERE adjustment > 100 OR adjustment < 0.01 OR close <= 0
 ORDER BY adjustment DESC LIMIT 8
""")
ext["adjustment"] = ext["adjustment"].map(lambda v: f"{v:.3g}")
ext.reset_index(drop=True)
```

**Findings.** (1) **No-trade placeholder rows:** 5.5% of price rows carry
`volume = 0` with a positive close — Sharadar bulk includes suspended /
no-trade days; of those, ~301k carry adjustment factors at the **8.5×10¹⁸
overflow sentinel** (e.g. `BINI`, 2015) because `closeadj` was not
populated for the row. (2) **The adjustment tail is mostly mechanical, not
corruption:** even among traded rows, ~1.8% have `adjustment > 100` — the
cumulative split+dividend rescale of long histories. The as-traded close
itself is unaffected, so **returns/factor work should use `close` directly**
and apply `adjustment` only for total-return series, screening `volume = 0`
and `adjustment` outliers. (3) Two rows with `close ≤ 0` exist — a
one-line cleanup candidate.

```{python}
#| label: freshness
fr = q("""
 SELECT m.`table` kind, COUNT(*) n, MAX(p.date) last_quote
 FROM prices p JOIN securities_master m ON m.ticker = p.ticker
 GROUP BY 1
""")
fr["n"] = fr["n"].map(fmt)
fr.columns = ["bucket", "rows", "last quote"]
fr.reset_index(drop=True)
```
